verified_claims: OS Terrain 50 is an open lower-resolution digital terrain model for Great Britain.
Grid and contour data are supplied as 10km by 10km tiles identified from the southwest National Grid corner.
The grid has regular 50m post spacing.
Each 10km ASCII tile contains 200 columns and 200 rows.
ASCII rows read west to east and subsequent rows move south from the northwest origin.
Grid values are calculated at pixel centres and reported to the nearest 0.1m.
The ASCII header includes ncols, nrows, lower-left coordinates and cellsize.
The accompanying GML carries grid location, spacing, vertical-reference and spatial-reference metadata.
Contour data has 10m standard intervals and includes spot heights and land-water boundaries.
Spot-height z values are rounded to zero decimal places and can represent genuine depressions rather than summits.
GML contour feature types include ContourLine, SpotHeight and LandWaterBoundary.
GML identifiers follow the os.t50.<tile>.<sequence> pattern and geometry identifiers add a .geom suffix.
Whole-tile refresh regenerates sequential identifiers, so identifiers are release-specific rather than permanently stable.
The GML coordinate reference is EPSG:27700 and spot-height propertyValue is height above Newlyn or another British height datum.
Candidate measurement requires exact TQ29 product bytes, tile metadata, row-column derivation, two unique cell values and checksum readback.
